Commentary.Commentary: However overcast the conditions may be, 123 does not look like a total which will cause tremors in the English camp. They should be out in a while and will be aiming to end this day with at the most 2 wickets down. Stay tuned...
For a brief period, it looked like Powell and Shai Hope are weathering the storm with a 56-run stand but once the latter was dismissed, the remaining 7 wickets fell for just 45 runs.

Cannot fathom what would be going through Jason Holder's mind at the moment. It was not as overcast at the toss but suddenly, when his team came out to bat, the clouds came looming in. For a brief period, it looked like Powell and Shai Hope are weathering the storm with a 56-run stand but once the latter was dismissed, the remaining 7 wickets fell for just 45 runs.

So it has taken England just a few moments after Tea to wrap up the innings. It was the story of two bowlers - Stokes and Anderson as the former took 6 wickets to end on top but it was Jimmy who started the rut with the wickets of Brathwaite and Kyle Hope. Roland-Jones helped himself with a couple as well.

OUT! Take a bow, Stokes! His third 6-fer in Tests! That's the final nail in the coffin! Fullish delivery outside off, curving in substantially. Gabriel attempts an agricultural slog over mid on but misses it completely to get his stumps rattled. Stokes is all smiles and these are his career-best figures in Tests. His teammates encircle to congratulate him. So two-in-two for the all-rounder which means he will be on a hat-trick when he will come out to bowl in the next innings. THE WINDIES ARE BOWLED OUT FOR 123!
SHANNON GABRIEL is the last man in.

OUT! What a catch from Anderson! He hands Stokes his 4th Test 5-fer! The all-rounder hits the deck hard around off and extracts extra bounce from the surface. Roach is taken aback by the bite. He looks to fend it away but gets a thick outside edge. Anderson at third slip dives to his left like a goalkeeper and takes a terrific catch.
Back of a length delivery outside off, seaming away after pitching. Roach keeps his bat inside the line and lets it go.
Another length delivery that nips away going past Devendra's hanging bat.
The batsman has attempted to put bat on ball but fails.
How did that miss the off stump? Anderson is too good for the tailender. On a fullish length on middle, swinging away. Bishoo has no choice but to play at it but is beaten comprehensively.
Close shave! The English bowlers are making the ball do the talking. Curving into Bishoo. He lets it go but the ball just goes past the off stump.
Prodigious movement again from outside off and seams away after hitting the deck. Devendra has no clue about it.
FOUR! Streaky runs! Good length delivery angling in from outside off. Bishoo looks to block it but gets a thick outside edge past gully to find the fence.
On a length outside off, swings back in substantially again. Roach looks to play at it but has to leave it in the end. Terrific over from Stokes.
Length delivery on off, straightens a bit after pitching. Roach is squared up and manages to get it off the outer half of the bat to point.
KEMAR ROACH is the new man in.

OUT! What a brute of a delivery from Stokes! Even a top order batsman would have found it really difficult to tackle it. Ben steams in and bowls it on a fuller length well outside off. It swings in prodigiously. Holder looks to keep it out gingerly but is beaten for pace and swing. The ball goes onto shatter the stumps. This is an absolute classic display of fast bowling. Very well-deserved!
Fuller in length outside off, nipping in. Holder shapes for the drive but bails out of it eventually.
In the length outside off, Holder doesn't fiddle with it.
Length delivery on leg stump, tucked to mid-wicket.
Ben Stokes to continue from the other end.
In the channel around off, holds its line this time. Bishoo lets it go. End of a testing over from Anderson.
Another beautiful delivery! On a length around off, shapes away after landing. Bishoo is opened up in his stance and is beaten all ends up.
Peach! Good length delivery on off, seams away substantially after pitching. Devendra keeps his bat inside the line and does well to leave it.
Around off, swinging away. Bishoo covers his stumps and makes a watchful leave. The inswinger is around the corner.
This one is on a length outside off and good seam position on that. The ball seams away after pitching. Bishoo points his bat skywards to allow it through.
Full length delivery well outside off, swinging away. Bishoo doesn't bother to play at that one.
Welcome back for the third session. A lot to look forward to. Here comes Jimmy Anderson with his tail up. Devendra Bishoo will face the first ball after tea. Four slips in place for him...
... Day 1, Session 3...

The Windies on the other hand looked absolutely clueless against the onslaught that was on offer. They are 7 down at the moment and by the looks of things, it seems like they won't even reach 150. Will the Windies' tail wag? Will we see Anderson getting his 500th Test scalp? We shall find out in a very short while....

Another brilliant session for England! They have continued from where they left off in the first session. They scalped 5 wickets in 34 overs and gave away just 84 runs in this session and are on the verge to bowl the tourists out. It was Toby Roland-Jones and Ben Stokes who led the way for their side. The latter in particular was really impressive in his extended spell as he got the ball to move both ways. James Anderson towards the end was called back but wasn't that effective. A worry for the hosts - Stuart Broad is off the field due to a sore ankle, let's hope it's nothing serious.
Sprays it down the leg side, Holder looks to work it away but fails to do so. IT'S TEA ON DAY 1!
Length ball outside off, Holder stands back and plays inside the line.
Fuller in length and getting it to curl away. Holder once again leans into it to drive but gets beaten once more.
FOUR! Edgyy! Fuller and bowled wide outside off, Holder once again drives it away from the body. Gets it off the outer half of the blade and rolls behind point for a boundary.

Edged and it's dropped! Joe Root is the culprit! Stokes is fuming at the moment. He comes running in and serves a length delivery on off. Holder plays it away from the body and that almost brings his downfall. An outside edge is induced but much to the batsman's delight, the English skipper at second slip dives to his left but spills the catch. A chance goes down abegging.
A bit short and outside off, Holder taps it in front of cover-point and sets off. Bishoo is quick to say a NO and send his skipper back.
Beaten again! On a length and curving away just enough to beat the blade. But not getting that edge he is waiting for. The wait continues as Tea is looming.
Goes full and wide outside off, Bishoo is not going to play at those. Anderson and Bishoo share a smile.
Goes from around the wicket and drops it on a good length around off. Bishoo has a tentative push inside the line and hence gets beaten.
Trying too much? Anderson once again bowls it wider outside off. The angle that he his opting to bowl is taking the ball further away from the batsman. Left alone.
Fuller and slanting away outside off, easy leave for Devendra.
Back of a length delivery, coming back in a bit, dealt with a straight blade.
Goes wide of the crease and drops it on the shorter side. Jason stays back and pushes it off the inner half back to Ben Stokes who shares some words of wisdom.
A bit short and hurled around off, Bishoo lunges forward and taps it towards cover for a brisk single.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Apparently Stuart Broad has gone off the field with a sore heel. Meanwhile, Moeen Ali has come back onto the field and is stationed at leg slip.
Sprays it too full and wide outside off to make the Windies leggie play at it.

How did that miss the stumps? That was mighty close! He's getting some real swing here. Keeps it full but it turns out to be a yorker which nips back in. Bishoo is late to bring his bat down as the ball nearly takes the off pole apart.
From around the wicket, fires it full and outside off, Bishoo shoulders his arms to that one.
Anderson sticks to his length, keeps it around off and induces an edge as well. However, the ball doesn't carry to Stokes stationed at fourth slip. Hands on head! A maiden for Jimmy!
Shortish and angling in, tucked towards the leg side.
What scenes. Every bowler would love this. As soon as Anderson comes steaming in the Lord's crowd is right behind him....
Fuller in length and swinging away sharply, Holder is tempted to go after it. Once again is beaten.
On a length around off, Holder once again strides forward but the ball straightens a touch to nearly take the outside edge.
Bowls it outside off, it curves away, Jason lunges forward to poke at it but is beaten all ends up. Oohhhs and Aaahsss follows!
On a length and served in the channel outside off, left alone by the Windies skipper.
He's back! A loud cheer from the crowd as JAMES ANDERSON is back into the attack. Can he reach the milestone we are all waiting for?
The leggie is happy to leave it alone this time.
Stokes goes over the wicket and angles it in from outside off. Bishoo plays inside the line of this.
Good length delivery, nipping back in from around off and hits DB on the thigh pad.

FOUR! Inside edge and through! Stokes is getting heavy swing but isn't able to control it. Fuller and angling in from around off, Bishoo brings his bat down to drive it away from the body but the ball takes the inside edge and dribbles down to the fine leg fence for a boundary.
Stokes oversteps! Very full and attacking the stumps. Bishoo stays leg side and jams it out. Umpire Erasmus signals it as a no ball as Stokes oversteps. He'll have to deliver it again.
Fuller again but this time the line is down the leg side. Devendra looks to flick but is undone by the pace on the ball. Bairstow behind the stumps does well to stop that one.
Stokes from around the wicket sprays it fuller and wide outside off. Bishoo has got nothing to offer to that one.
Moeen Ali is going off the field. This could also signal Jimmy Anderson to come on from his end.
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Another one outside off and Holder once again looks to go hard at it. He is not able to connect with the ball at all right now.
Flighted around off, Holder looks to play it through covers but misses.
Outside off, Holder opens the face of the bat and helps it to third man for a couple.
Loopy ball around off, played straight back to the bowler.
Floated around middle and off, Holder plays it straight to mid-wicket.
Very full and swinging into the batsman. Bishoo does well to keep it out.
Full outside off, Holder pushes it towards covers and sets off. That's a poor run by the skipper as a direct hit from Roland-Jones at the striker's end could have dismissed Bishoo.
Back of a length ball wide outside off. Easy leave for Holder.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.

Close! A good length ball around off, seams slightly away and goes just past the outside edge of Holder. He was looking to defend it off the back foot but could not get behind the line of the delivery.
Fuller outside off, Holder chooses to leave it alone.
Ends the over by defending this one off the back foot. It was tossed up around middle and off and Bishoo does well to keep it out.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Jimmy Anderson is loosening up, as he should be. He will be sensing to clean up the tail now.
Floats this one around off, Bishoo defends it towards the off side.
Loopy ball on middle, played straight back to the bowler.
Plays this one off the front foot and into the ground.
FOUR! Floated on off, Bishoo slashes hard at it and good thing that he does. The ball shoots off his outside edge past first slip towards the ropes. Lucky runs for Windies but they'll take them.
The batsman failed to make contact and was hit low on the pads. A strong appeal from the bowler and fielders. The Umpire decides the batsman is not out.
The batsman goes after this one but misses the line completely.
Outside off, left alone.
The batsman fails to put bat on ball.
Fuller around middle and off, Holder defends it off the front foot.
Going down the leg side, Holder goes for it but misses.
That ball has struck the batsman on the thigh-pad. The fielding side are asking the question.
Floated on middle, Bishoo defends it off the back foot solidly.
Gets right behind the line of the delivery and defends it.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
Flighted on off, Bishoo plays it straight towards point.
Floated on off, played off the front foot and into the ground towards covers for a single.
Ends the over by leaving the ball outside his off stump.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
DEVENDRA BISHOO is the new man in.

OUT! The catch is legal and Dowrich has to depart! Another one bites the dust. Like the previous dismissal, this one too seams slightly away from the batsman. Dowrich pushes inside the line and the ball takes the outside edge of the bat and goes low towards Cook at first slip. The former English skipper makes no mistake. The umpires want to check whether everything is fine and so refer it upstairs. The landing of the foot is fine according to the replays and it takes just one view for the third umpire S.Ravi to decide that the catch is perfectly legal. The decision stays as it is and the 7th wicket is down. So after dropping three catches in a row, Cook has bounced back with two catches and this one was a beauty. West Indies in danger of getting bowled out in this session itself.
That is a brilliant catch! Or is it? England are celebrating and so is Stokes. However, the umpires want to check the legality of the catch. Referred upstairs...
Good length ball on off, defended off the back foot towards covers for a single.
JASON HOLDER walks in to bat next. Can the skipper bail his side out of trouble?

OUT! That's a jaffa from Ben Stokes! He bowls a full length ball around off and it shapes slightly away. Chase looks to defend but this is just unplayable as the ball goes past his outside edge and strikes the off stump. Stokes is elated with this and he's really enjoying the movement he's getting off the pitch. The first ball was an inswinger and this time the away swinger does the trick for him and his side.
Full outside off, Dowrich pushes it through the covers for a single. 100 up for the visitors.
Pushes this one off the back foot to end the over.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Floats this on middle, Chase defends it off the back foot.
Loopy ball on off, driven through the covers for a couple.
Floated on middle and off, Chase defends it off the back foot.
FOUR! Outside off, Chase goes for it but the ball takes an outside edge and goes through the slip region for a boundary. Almost a wicket in the first ball itself.
MOEEN ALI is introduced into the attack. Pretty interesting tactics. Ben Stokes is bowling from the end of Toby Roland-Jones, so either it is a change of end for him and Stokes or something else.
Wide down the leg side, No trouble at all for the batsman.
No ball. On a good length outside off, Dowrich looks to defend it but gets an outside edge which falls short of the slip fielder.
Wide down the leg side this time. Dowrich does not go for it.

Good length but this time nipping into the batsman. Dowrich is caught off guard as he looks to flick it away. The ball takes an inside edge and thuds onto this pads. That could easily have been an LBW there!
The batsman chooses to leave the ball outside his off stump.
Fuller just outside off, the ball seams away after pitching as well. Dowrich looks to drive but misses as the ball goes just past his outside edge.
Another one outside off, Dowrich shoulders his arms and lets it through.
The ball is way outside the off stump, easy leave for the batsman.
FOUR! Short ball and it has been put away. Chase rocks onto his back foot and pulls it through fine leg for a boundary. The fielder in the deep is way too wide and could not get there to make a stop.
Another full length ball just outside off. Chase pushes it down the ground but TRJ does really well to get down and make the stop to his leg.
Full around off and middle, played straight back to the bowler off the front foot.
Another fuller length ball outside off. Chase leaves it alone.
Fuller on off, Chase plays it straight to point.
Leg bye. This one is also going down the leg side. It brushes off his pads and goes towards fine leg. Single sneaked through and the umpire signals Leg Bye.
Another one going down leg, Chase leaves it alone.
Wide down the leg side, No trouble at all for the batsman.
On the pads this time, Chase flicks it and the ball ball falls just short of the fielder at short leg.
Good length ball on middle and off, Chase defends it.
Bowls this on middle, Chase plays it straight to mid-wicket.
Good length ball around middle and off, defended off the back foot.
Gets right behind the line of the delivery and defends it solidly.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Very full from TRJ, Dowrich gets his bat down in time to block it out.
Fuller on off, Dowrich plays it straight to point.
Bowls this outside off, Dowrich leaves it alone.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.

Another one that takes an inside edge. This is on middle and leg and Chase looks to defend it. The ball takes the inside edge and thuds onto his pads. The fielders ask the question but the umpire shows no interest.
Back of a length outside off. Chase looks to leave it late but the ball takes an edge and falls short of the fielder at third slip.
This one is fuller but outside off, Chase leaves it alone.

Back of a length ball angling down leg. Chase looks to clip it down the leg side but but misses. The ball clips his thigh pad and the keeper takes the catch. The fielders go up to appeal but the umpire shows no interest as that went off the pad.
Length ball outside off, left alone.
Fuller on middle, Dowrich looks to drive it but gets an inside edge to mid-wicket.
Gets to his back foot and shows the full face of the bat and defends it solidly.
Full and wide outside off, Dowrich leaves it alone.
Good length ball on middle, played off the back foot towards mid-wicket.
Drinks are on the field. Meanwhile, SHANE DOWRICH has walked in to replace Blackwood.

OUT! Bowled 'em! Blackwood plays all round this full length delivery shaping in from off. He was looking to slog it across the line but misses the ball completely. The ball goes through his bat and pad and castles onto his middle stump. The Windies are in trouble now with half their side back in the hut!
Length ball around off, tapped off the back foot towards point.
Bowls this around middle, defended solidly by Chase off the back foot.
Once again leaves the ball outside off.
Another one bowled outside off. Chase wants nothing to do with it.
Wide outside off, easy leave for Chase.
Good length outside off, Chase looks to prod at it but misses.
Short leg comes in.
Full on middle, Blackwood pushes it through the covers for a single to get off the mark.
Another one outside off, Chase leaves it alone.
Full on middle, Chase drives it straight back.
Length ball, Chase gets behind the line of the delivery and defends it off the back foot.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
FOUR! Good length ball on middle and this time Chase flicks it through mid-wicket for a boundary.

FOUR! Angles this one from over the wicket on middle and leg. Chase looks to clip it fine but end up edging it onto his pads off the inside half of the bat. The ball brushes off the pads and races away to the fine leg fence.
This one swings the other way. Jermaine keeps his calm and leaves it alone. A testing and a successful over from Stokes comes to an end.
Swinging in sharply from outside off, Blackwood covers his off pole and allows it through safely.
JERMAINE BLACKWOOD walks in to bat next.

OUT! England are on top once again! This time it is Stokes who provides another breakthrough in quick succession. Keeps this one full and straight in line of the stumps. Powell goes for a drive down the ground but doesn't bother keeping it down. Ben in his followthrough bends, maintains his balance and grabs a very good catch. A resolute knock from the southpaw comes to an end. He pays the price for driving with minimal foot movement. He is absolutely gutted with himself. Can the home side trigger a collapse now?
Another one outside off and the southpaw doesn't show any interest to play again.
In the zone outside off, Kieran doesn't fiddle with it.
Fuller length delivery around off, swinging away. Powell lets it go.
ROSTON CHASE is the new man in.

OUT! The hero of the last match has been dismissed! England will be delighted with this, both the dangermen have been removed. First it was Brathwaite and now it's Shai Hope. This is bowled on a good length outside off and Hope looks to defend it tentatively off the back foot. The ball seams slightly away after pitching, bounces a tad extra and takes the outside edge of Hope's bat. Cook at first slip takes the catch and is proud of himself. He has been dropping catches on a consistent basis since the last match and will be relieved not to make a mistake this time.
Going down the leg side, Hope looks to clip it away but misses.
FOUR! Delightful shot from Hope. This is served full outside off and Hope gets on his front foot to drive it through the covers.
Gets right behind the line of the delivery and defends this off the back foot.
The wind has picked up at Lord's at the moment. Hopefully, it will blow away the dark clouds as well.
Another one that has been defended off the back foot by Hope. This is bowled on a length on off as well.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Short ball from stokes this time. Powell looks to hook it behind but the ball goes over his head.
Full and outside off, Powell leaves it alone.
Another one outside off, Powell leaves it alone.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Full on off, Powell drives it straight down the ground. Stokes does really well to dive to his left and stop the ball.
Looks to drive this one from outside off. The ball swings swings away and beats the outside edge of the bat.
The batsman defends it from within the crease.
This time Hope leaves the ball outside off alone.
Hope looks to go for the one outside off. He was looking to guide it towards third man but failed to meet the ball.
50-run partnership comes up between Powell and Hope. These two have played sensible cricket and are providing a good foundation for the middle order to capitalize on.

Fuller on middle and leg. Powell flicks it through mid-wicket and takes three runs. Good chase by the fielder who prevents a boundary. Superb batting by these two as they get their first 50-run stand.
Another one outside off that has been left alone by Powell.
Outside off, Powell leaves it alone.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Full on middle, played through mid wicket for a single.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.
Back of a length this time, Powell defends it off the back foot.
Another one swung into the pads, played through mid wicket for a couple.

FOUR! Edgy from Powell! Bowls a fullish length ball on middle and the ball swings away as well. Powell looks to defend it but gets an outside edge which flies past backward point and races away to the fence. Lucky for Powell, Stokes will not mind that.
Ben Stokes is introduced into the attack.
Once again the ball outside off has been left alone by Hope.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
FOUR! Good length around leg. Hope flicks it nicely through mid-wicket for a boundary. The slope certainly helps Hope as the ball makes it way to the ropes.
Fuller outside off, Hope goes for it but misses.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Very, very full from Roland-Jones. Powell gets to his front foot and drives it magnificently through mid off. Good chase by the fielder at wide mid off to save a run for his team. Three runs taken.

Nasser Hussain on air makes another good analysis. He says that Powell's front foot is pretty stiff while he is driving. He doesn't show much decisive footwork and that is the reason he has been beaten on several occasions. In contrast, Ben Stokes is much more confident and he commits himself completely while driving. He gets the desired results as well.
Good length this time, Hope gets behind the line and defends it from within the crease.
Wide outside off stump, the batsman leaves it alone.
Fuller from Broad, Hope defends it off the front foot and into the ground.

Shout for LBW! Not given by the umpire. This is a good length ball on middle and leg, nips in sharply. Hope looks to defend it off the back foot. He misses and the ball strikes him on the thigh pad. Perhaps the height factor saved him there. Good shout nevertheless. Broad was interested in a review but Root knew that it was probably a touch too high.
FOUR! Angles this one down the leg side. Hope flicks it superbly fine down the leg side. The ball races away to the fine leg fence.
The batsman has played that off the front foot and into the ground.
Outside off from TRJ, Powell plays it straight to point.
Full and on the leg side. Powell tries tucking it behind but misses and the ball strikes him on the thigh pad.
Full on middle, Powell drives it straight to mid on.
This is on middle and off, Powell defends it solidly off the back foot.

Another one that beats the outside edge of the bat. Powell has not looked comfortable at all with the balls outside off. This was also full outside off and Powell could not connect with his attempt to play at it.
Flashy! TRJ bowls a full length ball just outside off. Powell looks to play a drive through the covers but misses the ball completely.
Fuller just outside off. Hope looks to defend but is tentative and misses it in the end. He is lucky that he did not get an edge there.
Good length ball around middle and leg. Hope gets behind the line to defend it.
Good length ball wide outside off. Once again, Hope does not go for it.
Another one outside off which Hope ignores.
The batsman shoulders arms to let that one through.

Nasser Hussain on air mentions that Kieran Powell is playing much better today. In Headingley, he was hurrying into his strokes and as a result, wasn't getting his timing right. Today, he is taking his time and allowing the ball to come which is a much better way to play.
Good length ball on middle and off, Hope defends it off the back foot.
Goes for the one outside off. The ball swings away from the outside edge. Another play and a miss by Powell!
Fuller this time, Powell defends it off his front foot.
Powell shoulders arms to let that one through.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
FOUR! Easy does it for Powell! He gets a short length ball outside off and Powell cuts it off the back foot through covers for a boundary.
Bowls this full on the pads, Hope clips it towards fine leg for a single.
Toby Roland-Jones replaces Anderson.
Ends the over by leaving the ball outside off. He could do that all day.
Fuller this time on off, Powell plays it to mid-wicket.
Another one outside off, left alone.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
On a good length, Powell defends it off the back foot.
Bowls this outside off and Powell does not look to play at it.
This time Hope offers no shot at the ball outside off.
Play and a miss this time! This is a superb delivery from Anderson. Bowls it around middle and gets the ball to move away from the outside edge of the bat. That was close!

FOUR! Another superb shot through the covers. Anderson once again bowls a fuller length delivery outside off. Hope is confident now and creams it through the covers for the second boundary of the over.
Back of a length, defended off the back foot.
FOUR! Not that convincing but effective! Full length delivery outside off, swinging away. Hope leans ahead a touch and drives it with an open face past point to find the fence.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Superb shot from the southpaw. This is full outside off and Powell simply pushes it off his front foot towards the long off fence.

Edged but safe! Broad bowls a good length ball just outside off and Powell tries to defend it with soft hands. Gets an outside edge but falls short of the man at fourth slip. He needs to be more careful.
Fuller this time, Powell defends it off the front foot.
Gets right behind the line of this delivery to defend it.
Defended off the front foot by the batsman presenting the full face of the bat.
Bowls this one on a good length outside off. Powell leaves it alone.
Stuart Broad to bowl from the other end.
Full on off, Hope drives it straight to mid off.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Peach! Outside off on a shortish length, Hope feels for it but gets beaten all ends up. He is lucky that he didn't nick that.
On the pads this time, Powell flicks it away off the inner half behind square leg for a single.
The batsman lets the ball go outside his off stump.
Bowls an inswinging delivery on the leg stump, Powell looks to flick it but misses and is struck on the pads. No real appeal from the Englishmen as it was heading down leg.

The players are walking back out to the middle for the second session. James Anderson to continue with the ball. An important update - Tea will be taken at 1610 local time due to the rain stoppage in the first session.
... Day 1, Session 2...

The star of the previous game, Shai Hope is looking confident from the word go. Kieran Powell has been very patient and is playing a key role from the other end. The conditions are still overcast and the seam bowlers need to make it count. There was a slight rain stoppage but thankfully, it didn't last long. However, dark clouds are still looking threatening and we can only hope that they will stay away. Join us in a while for the afternoon session.

A good session for England! Their senior most pro, James Anderson has been right on the money and is just one shy of 500 Test wickets - a rare feat indeed. He has bowled testing lines and lengths and made the ball do the talking. Brathwaite was dropped on 3 but it didn't cost the home side much. He continued to be tentative and Anderson nipped him out. Kyle Hope also struggled to get going and gifted his wicket away.
Fuller and swinging away, Shai Hope lunges forward and then lifts his bat to make another leave. LUNCH ON DAY 1!
Fuller and sprayed outside off, Hope ignores.
Back of a length delivery outside off, Shai hangs back in defense.
Tad fuller and served around the off stump line, Shai Hope lunges forward in defense.
Fuller and strayed down the leg side. The batsman tries helping it on its way but fails to do so.
On a good length and shaping away from outside off. The length is such that it allows the batsman to let it be.

Just a minute left for the break. Jonny Bairstow rushes across to the other end to ensure that there is one more over bowled in this session. The clock on the ground is showing 12.59 but Michael Holding on air says that more often than not the umpires check their wrist watches. Here comes Roland-Jones.
A bit fuller and served wider outside off, Kieran leaves it alone.
Back to out-swingers again. No harm in leaving them alone.
There it is! He is setting him up here. Beware Powell! Brings it back into the left-hander but KP stands behind the line and offers a straight bat defense.
Once again bowls it outside off and it moves further away. Easy peasy leave for the southpaw.
Slants it across the left-hander who has no issue in letting it be.
Bowls it on middle and it jags away with the angle as Powell sees it go past him to the keeper.
Hope shoulders arms to let that one through.
Beaten! That's more like it! A fuller ball, curling away off the deck and tempts Hope to go for it. The batsman does so and gets beaten all ends up.
Listens to me and pitches it right up there. Shai Hope offers no stroke.
Length delivery outside off, defended off the back foot. He should be bowling much fuller.
Ahead of a length and around off, all the time in the world for Hope to keep that one out.
Begins his spell with a back of a length delivery outside off, punched through covers for an easy single.
TOBY ROLAND-JONES is brought into the attack now.
Fuller and swinging in on the pads, Hope walks across a touch and flicks it towards mid-wicket. A maiden for Jimmy!
Pitches it on a fuller length outside off, SH stabs it into the ground.
On a length and outside off, this one kicks off the deck. Hope hangs his bat out in defense but once again gets beaten.
Good length delivery on off, Shai Hope has a tentative poke inside the line. Luckily, he didn't nick that one.
Toby Roland-Jones is warming up.
Around off, curling away, no harm for Shai to make a leave.
Serves it fuller outside off, Hope takes his front foot across to block it down on the pitch.
Marginally overpitched around off, Powell brings his bat down at the angle but drives it straight to the fielder at short cover.
Fuller on middle and leg, worked towards mid on.
Fuller and swinging further away, Powell lets it be.
The ball is too wide on the off side for the batsman to make any contact.
Fuller and outside off, nicely left alone.
FOUR! Fuller and swinging back in on the pads, Powell uses the pace of the ball and clips it behind square on the leg side for a boundary.
FOUR! Easily done! Slants it away on a length outside off, Hope stands tall, opens the face of the bat and dabs it past fourth slip to find the fence again. Good positive start from Shai!
Good length delivery outside off, once again defended nicely off the back foot.

FOUR! Shot, that! Continuing from where he left off? Anderson actually shouldn't be worried with that. He sticks to a fuller ball outside off, Hope lunges ahead and drives it on the up through covers. Pierces the gap and finds the fence. That's some way to get off the mark.
SHAI HOPE walks in next, replacing his brother. He was the star of the previous game and with his side in early trouble, can he replicate it?

OUT! Anderson is up and running! Wicket number 499 for the veteran! He keeps it fuller around off, Kyle Hope leans ahead to play at that but then at the last moment decides not to do so. His bat is hanging out and the ball takes the outside edge and flies towards first slip. However, Jonny Bairstow dives full length to his right and takes it near the face of Alastair Cook. A typical Anderson celebration follows - right arm up with a finger pointing skywards. Oh wait, they are checking for the no ball. But much to the bowler's delight, the front foot is fine. Another failure for Kyle Hope as he walks back dejected.
Angles it in from around off, defended solidly off the front foot.
Fuller and a bit wide outside off, Hope has got nothing to do with that one.
Fires in a fuller ball on the pads, Powell misses his attempted flick shot and wears it on the pads. No real appeal as it was going down leg.
Pitches it on a length outside off and straightens off the deck to beat Powell.
This is much better from Broad. He persists to bowl it outside the off stump. Kieran Powell shows patience and leaves it alone.
Gets his front foot across and stabs it straight towards the point fielder.
Hits the deck hard and hurls it around the off stump channel, Kieran lifts his bat to let it be.
FOUR! Broad begins the spell from around the wicket and straightaway offers a gift. Strays on the pads and it's easily flicked away through mid-wicket for a boundary by Powell.
Stuart Broad to have a go from the other end...
In the channel outside off, Hope lets it be.
Arrows in a good length delivery on middle and off, defended gently off the front foot.
Similar delivery! Serves it on a length and then gets it to move away beating the outside edge of Kyle Hope's bat.
On a length and angling in from around off, Hope has a push at it but the ball nips away to nearly take the outside edge.
Pitches it up again, Hope lunges forward and blocks it off the front foot.
Starts off with a fuller ball, moving away nicely. Kyle Hope watches it till the last moment before making a leave.
The players are back. The weather is still gloomy but let's hope it clears out soon. KYLE HOPE and KIERAN POWELL to continue their innings. JAMES ANDERSON to continue with the ball. Here we go...
UPDATE 1210 local time - Good news! The rain has stopped and the umpires are out having a check. The covers are also being removed. Play should resume in about 20 minutes.

This was more or less coming. Mike Atherton on air is hopeful that this is just a passing shower and adds that the forecast is not that bad. It is not raining heavily but they are not continuing for now. Stay tuned for updates...

There is a lot of delay to bowl this over. Gaffaney is not particularly keen to continue because it has gone really dark and the drizzle is getting heavier. Anderson is smiling but no one is getting a move on. Okay the decision is taken. THE PLAYERS ARE WALKING OFF.
The batsman shows the full face of the bat and defends the ball off the back foot.
Landed on a good length outside off, not played at again. Broad needs to be closer.
One more leave outside off.
Rain drops on the camera lens... the umbrellas are opening up in the stands...
On a good length around off, watchfully defended.
Outside off, left alone.
Umpire Marais Erasmus has a chat with Chris Gaffaney about the lights. Should the stadium lights be switched on? It is looking really gloomy out there. But nothing from the umpires as of now.
Landed around off, watchfully defended.
Full on middle, pushed towards mid on.
Outside off, left alone.
KYLE HOPE walks in at number 3, replacing Brathwaite.

OUT! Caught behind! Wicket number 498 for Jimmy in Tests! He is pumped up. His perseverance has paid dividends. He has been toiling, toiling, toiling for the last 45 minutes and eventually gets the edge. He has been bowling mainly inswingers but this one goes away from the batsman. Brathwaite has a tentative poke, perhaps expecting the inswinger. But instead he gets a thick nick behind to Jonny Bairstow who collects and jumps in jubilation. West Indies have lost their first quickly after surviving some really torrid 45 minutes.
Fishing... Brathwaite pokes at that one slightly outside off and is beaten.
One more leave outside off.
Outside off, left alone.
Outside off, left alone.
Another indipper, but down the leg side, Kieran misses his flick and is hit on the pads.
Outside off, left alone.

Nasser Hussain on air remarks on the lengths to be bowled on this pitch. Not necessarily here but mostly in England. Surprisingly, amongst the English bowlers, it has been Toby Roland-Jones who has been the fullest with 28 percent of his deliveries being on the fuller side. Anderson, on the other side, has been only bowling 13 percent of his deliveries this summer on that length. It has reflected as well with TRJ getting plenty of wickets this summer. Even today, the batsmen have been comfortable whenever the length has been short. But the moment the ball is pitched up, the batsmen are getting squared up.
This is down the leg side, flicked away for a single.
This one swings in, Kraigg looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads.
A rare full ball from Broad, puts it just around off, then gets it to move away. Brathwaite pushes but misses.
Full and around off, watchfully defended.
Landed outside off, shaping away, Kieran pokes at it with soft hands and dabs it to gully.

Another quick single. This is good running from West Indies and nice thinking too. Runs are hard to come by and rotation of strike will frustrate the bowler. This time he just pushes one to cover and takes one more.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, pushed through the covers. The fielders come charging in but Powell still goes for the single. Chancy run but he makes it.

Beautiful bowling. Broad needs to take a lesson or two from Jimmy. He bowls this really full, lands it around middle and then gets it to swing in. Powell looks to flick but gets a thick inside edge onto his pads.
Outside off, a play and a miss to end a very ordinary over. Broad has not made the batsmen play much at all. His lines have predominantly been wide.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket.
On a length but wide outside off, gets it to move away but Brathwaite never looked to play at that. Kept his bat well inside the line.
Outside off, pushed through the covers for a couple.
Goes back and tucks it to the covers for a single.
Whoa... one look at the dark grey clouds from the end where James Anderson is bowling and it gives us the creeps. Seems like the heavens may open anytime soon.
Landed outside off, left alone.
Landed around off, watchfully blocked.
Goes back and tucks it through the leg side for a couple.
This time he stays deep in his crease and blocks.
Around off, watchfully defended.
The batsman has defended it by getting right behind the line of the delivery.
Full and outside off, driven straight back.
Outside off, left alone.
FOUR! Nicely done. Welcome runs for the Windies. A length ball outside off, Powell waits for the ball to come to him and then guides it to the third man fence.

HOW DID THAT MISS? Tremendous, tremendous bowling. Broad bowls this on a length and the line is well outside off. Powell, assuming that it is going to be a successor of the ones before, lets it go. However, to his dismay, the ball comes in a long way. Luckily for him, it goes over the stumps.
Fuller and miles outside off, left alone.
Defended off the back foot by the batsman.
Landed outside off, but pretty wide, left alone.
Gets his radar slightly wrong this time, Powell flicks this through mid-wicket for a single.
Wider outside off, easier leave.
Another lovely delivery, almost similar to the one bowled previously. Only this time the line is outside off and is comfortably left alone.

That is a peach. Anderson keeps this really full and invites Powell to drive. The batsman obliges but does not move his feet at all. Prodigious movement away from him takes the ball past the outside edge. Brilliant bowling.
On a length this time, outside off, angling away, left alone.
Outside off, pushed through the covers for a single.

Finally makes the batsman play, by bowling it on a length from around the wicket, then getting it to come back in. Powell looks to flick but misses and is hit on the pads. A mild LBW shout ensues but that seemed to be going down leg.
Keep counting. Five dots on the trot, all made contact directly by the keeper. The batsman has had nothing to do with any of those.
Make that four leaves in a row now.
Fuller in length, outside off again, left alone once more.
On a good length outside off, left alone again.
Landed outside off, angling away, let through.
On middle and leg, flicked straight to short mid-wicket. Eventful over. Could have had a wicket on more than one occasion.
Shorter in length this time, KB thinks there are some freebies on offer, slashes hard but misses.

ANOTHER EDGE! This one does not go to hand. This is on a length again, outside off, Kraigg pushes at it tentatively once more and gets another outside edge. However, luckily for him, it does not carry to the diving Ben Stokes at gully.

EDGED, DROPPED! It is Cook. One of the safest fielders in the slip cordon. But he has shelled one. And this is not new. He put down two in the previous Test too. Anderson bowls a beautiful delivery, landing it on a length outside off and gets it to curve away. Brathwaite is forced to defend coming forward but then gets squared up as the ball moves away. It takes the outside edge and goes straight to Alastair Cook at first slip who gets down to catch but then puts it down. Shai Hope and Brathwaite were the beneficiaries in the previous game.
Fuller outside off, Powell looks to flick it away but gets a leading edge through the covers. A single taken.
Landed on a good length around off, defended from the crease.
Better than the previous one, closer to the stumps, let through.
Anti-climax. This is sprayed wide outside off, Brathwaite lets it go.
Much, much fuller, around off, that is the length to bowl, KB comes forward and blocks it out.
Stays back in his crease this time and blocks.
This is much fuller around off, Brathwaite comes forward and defends.
Good length ball on middle, defended from within the crease.
Stuart Broad to bowl from the other end.
Fuller around off, Brathwaite taps it towards covers for a single.
Another one outside off, Brathwaite taps it towards point watchfully.
Bowls this slightly wide outside off. Brathwaite does not go for it.
Forces the batsman to play this one. On a good length around off, Brathwaite defends it off the front foot and into the ground.
Good length outside off, Brathwaite leaves it alone.
Starts off with a good length ball around off. Punched through the covers off the back foot for a brace.

The players are out in the middle as KRAIGG BRATHWAITE and KIERAN POWELL take their guard. JAMES ANDERSON to open the bowling for the hosts. He is on 497 wickets! Conditions are a little overcast but hopefully there will be no rain. Three slips and a gully in place, here we go!
WEST INDIES WIN THE TOSS AND WILL BAT FIRST. Team changes - As announced last evening, the hosts bring in Toby Roland-Jones in place of Chris Woakes. West Indies remain unchanged.

Hello and welcome to the third and final Test match between England and West Indies. The hosts were given a wake-up call after Windies shocked everyone with a win at Headingley. It was the brilliance of Kraigg Brathwaite and Shai Hope (with the bat) that handed the visitors their first victory in 17 years on English soil. They will hope to win their second consecutive Test away from home after a very long time. So it all sets up for a thrilling decider at the Mecca of cricket - Lord's. Stay tuned for the toss.
